headline: High: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and run shell commands, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with a non-isolated game agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the filesystem and use clipboard/stdin, while godot_rl_agents has no isolation or provenance controls shown. A shared file or copied output can therefore be treated as trusted input by Open Interpreter, creating an injection path. The pathway is inferred from the pair, not directly documented.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through a shared file, clipboard, or stdin/stdout bridge
IF Open Interpreter is run with default confirmation behavior and parses agent_a output as instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate directories
Require a human to review any text passed from agent_a to agent_b
Run Open Interpreter in Docker or another isolated environment
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents is a local game-playing agent with no stated data controls. If agent_a artifacts or local secrets are present on disk, agent_b can read and potentially transmit them. This is a default-capable leakage path, though not proven for a specific secret class.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared local filesystem
IF Open Interpreter is pointed at directories containing agent_a outputs or secrets
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the working directory
Run Open Interpreter with a restricted workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing
Disable network egress for the session if possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or shell capabilities, but agent_b can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same workspace, agent_b can overwrite or race with agent_a artifacts, and the concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. The conflict is therefore default-dangerous for shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF agent_b is allowed to write while agent_a is producing artifacts
mitigations: Give each agent a separate working directory
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repository
Use git branches or commits for handoff instead of shared files
Pause agent_b before agent_a writes final outputs
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator mutex

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and modify files, so if it consumes agent_a outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into real actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing agent, but the pair still creates a path where generated content becomes executable instructions or code. Because agent_b has action-taking authority by default, the blast radius is irreversible enough for high severity.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as code, commands, or configuration without verification
IF agent_b is run with --auto_run or equivalent auto-execution
mitigations: Require manual review before execution
Disable auto-run modes
Insert a validation step between agents
Limit agent_b to dry-run mode for handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for agent_a outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, while Open Interpreter can touch anything on the local machine and send data to configured model providers. The pair therefore has a plausible compliance gap if regulated data is present, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdictional violation. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is configured to send that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Exclude regulated folders from the workspace
Use a local-only model provider
Review retention settings for the provider
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency controls
